 Help is available for Pennsylvanians struggling with home heating costs.
 Starting Nov. 2, a statewide source of assistance, the federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, or LIHEAP, begins taking applications.
 The program, which is administered by the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, has income eligibility limits and offers cash and crisis grants that do not have to be paid back.
 Current annual household income limits and size for the program are: one person, up to $23,940; two people, $32,460; three people, $40,980; four people, $49,500. For every additional person, add $8,520.
 Local News 
 'I almost fell over': Rising heating oil bills force painful budget choices for Lancaster County customers 
 CHAD UMBLE | Staff Writer 
 Through LIHEAP, a household can typically receive one cash grant each heating season. Households can receive more than one crisis grant each heating season if they meet the income guidelines and are in jeopardy of having their heating utility service terminated, have already had their heating utility service terminated, or who are out of or have less than two weeks’ worth of deliverable fuel, such as fuel oil, propane, coal or wood.
 Last year, the cash grant minimum was $200, and the maximum cash grant was $1,000. Crisis grants ranged from $25 to $1,000. Details have not yet been released for this year.
 Once LIHEAP goes live Nov. 2, residents can learn more and apply at www.compass.state.pa.us , by calling the LIHEAP Client Helpline at 1-866-857-7095 or by calling their local County Assistance Office.

 Both of the primary public utilities serving Lancaster County – UGI for natural gas and PPL for electricity – operate their own programs to aid customers struggling with their bills.
 UGI has programs that offer cash grants, free installation of energy conservation measures, and payment caps and forgiveness based on income.
 Eligibility and application processes may vary. For more information, call 1-800-UGI-WARM (1-800-844-9276).
 Denver-based UGI has more than 740,000 customers in 46 counties in Pennsylvania, including about 75,000 residential natural gas customers in Lancaster County. About 34% of Lancaster County homes heat with natural gas, making it the second most common heating fuel here, according to the U.S. Census 2024 American Community Survey.
 PPL has programs that offer cash grants, free installation of energy conservation measures, and payment caps and forgiveness based on income.
 Eligibility and application processes may vary. For more information, call 800‑342‑5775.
 PPL serves about 272,000 customers in Lancaster County, where about 37% of homes heat with electricity, making it the most common heating fuel here, according to the U.S. Census 2024 American Community Survey.
